Delegates: Group delegation, We Love Oakville - George Niblock and Jim Goodfellow.
Mayor Knoll passed the Chair to Councillor Admas at 6:43 p.m.
Councillor Adams passed the Chair back to Mayor Knoll at 6:58 p.m.
Moved by
Mayor Knoll
Seconded by
Councillor Haslett-Theall
WHEREAS
pursuant to Orders-in-Council 1499/25, 1502/25, 1503/25, and 1504/25, each of the following four sites in the Town of Oakville below has been designated transit-oriented community lands under section 2 of the
Transit-Oriented Communities Act, 2020
:
217 and 227 Cross Avenue, and 571, 581, 587-595 Argus Rd
157 and 165 Cross Avenue
166 South Service Road East
590 Argus Road
WHEREAS
pursuant to Order-in-Council 589/25, the Minister of Infrastructure shares authority, with the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, to make Minister Zoning Orders under s. 47 (1) (a) of the
Planning Act
for transit-oriented community lands;
WHEREAS
on April 9, 2026, the Minister of Infrastructure issued four Minister’s Zoning Orders (MZOs) for the transit-oriented community lands in the Town of Oakville, as Zoning Orders 01-2026, 02-2026, 03-2026, and 04-2026 (TOC lands);
WHEREAS
the MZOs for the TOC lands permit buildings of up to 56 storeys; however,  the province included a statement in the announcement of the MZOs:
In response to feedback received from the town and the community, Ontario is working with the municipality and impacted partners on further refinements to the Oakville TOC that will result in building heights of 38 storeys, while maintaining the overall number of homes and community benefits.
WHEREAS
NAV CANADA has advised landowners and the Town of Oakville that it has objections to several development proposals in Midtown Oakville, including the TOC lands, and, in particular, buildings and/or construction cranes that exceed 780 feet above sea level, will have impacts on NAV CANADA’s Minimum Vectoring Altitude, which are specific altitudes used by air traffic controllers to provide safe, orderly and expeditious movements of aircraft that operate in the airspace that surrounds the Toronto Pearson Airport and Billy Bishop Toronto City Airport;
WHEREAS
the public remains deeply concerned with the imposition of MZOs and lack of action to approve OPA 70 which is the result of comprehensive land use planning including public consultation and establishes a clear vision for the growth of Midtown;
WHEREAS
Council remain committed to responsible growth in Midtown as demonstrated by the approval of development at 420 South Service Road;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED:
THAT Council requests the Minister of Infrastructure revoke Zoning Orders 01-2026, 02-2026, 03-2026, and 04-2026 for the TOC lands;
THAT Council requests that the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing approve OPA 70 as adopted by Council, without delay, and without modifications to conform OPA 70 to the MZOs, and
THAT the confidential direction approved by Council on March 23, 2026 related to the TOC lands be revoked.
For (14)
Mayor Knoll, Councillor Adams, Councillor Caldwell, Councillor Elliott, Councillor Grant, Councillor Haslett-Theall, Councillor Lapworth, Councillor Lishchyna, Councillor Longo, Councillor McNeice, Councillor Nanda, Councillor Saunders, Councillor Wubbenhorst,  and Councillor Xie
Absent (1)
Councillor Chisholm
CARRIED (14 to 0)
